the census reads every list a graph editor binds, and stops reading C++ as text: closes debt-census-surfaces-are-still-incomplete, all three axes. AXIS 1 -- the debt said three UE command lists were missing and the real answer was EIGHT, because the unit is the TCommands CLASS and not the header: visual script editor commands.h holds three classes and only one is the graph's, BehaviorTreeEditorCommands.h holds three, and R1603's single list happened to be one class per file so the difference was invisible. 152 rows judged across visual script editor commands 36, FMaterialEditorCommands 68, FAnimGraphCommands 19, FSoundCueGraphEditorCommands 10, FSoundClassEditorCommands 4 and the three behaviour-tree classes 15. Scope is now DECLARED: every TCommands class under Engine/Source/Editor (90 of them) is either read or excluded BY NAME with a reason, and one in neither is a finding, so the next list Epic adds cannot be quietly outside the denominator. THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE AND THAT IS THE FINDING: 20/51 = 39% became 45/113 = 39% and the engine held at 40% overall, so the generic canvas was representative -- while the per-editor split is not (MaterialEditor 58, visual script editor 38, BehaviorTreeDebugger 22, AnimGraph 16). AXIS 2 measured rather than argued and the tool re-derives it every run: of 36 GetNodeContextMenuActions overrides, 17 register a command from a TCommands list (the same unit, now in the denominator) and 16 build an FUIAction on the spot, which has no name anywhere to key a row on. AXIS 3 stays with self-correction, except that two verdicts were settled by reading the call site: SoundCue's ToggleSolo/ToggleMute reach the audio debugger's ToggleSoloSoundCue on the ASSET, so they are app-content rather than a node bypass. THE DCC HALF IS THE BIGGER CORRECTION, and it came from the user asking whether reading C++ as text is good enough. It is not, and asking the census to account for EVERY  token rather than to find the ones it knew how to find surfaced four things at once: a FIFTH registration mechanism (NOD_socket_items_ops.hh registers 69 operator ids through four templates whose idnames live as static constexpr StringRefNull members in a different directory, so no registration site writes ot->idname at all -- and the DCC's own comment says the string is spelled out "so that it is more searchable", meaning the reference anticipated a text census and this one still missed it); a receiver that is not called ot (operator_type->idname, which is debt-DCC-census-by-field-name recurring INSIDE the tool built to end it); an id spelled __func__, which no text scan can read; and a registration FUNCTION whose symbol is not an operator id at all (collapse_toggle registers hide_toggle, so counting the symbol would have invented one). The DCC's live census goes 170 -> 246 and its coverage 75% -> 71%, operator 78% -> 73%. A new verdict, instance, is composition in the other direction: 69 instantiations of four behaviours are FOUR rows in the denominator, judged once at the maker, because counting them all would put one capability there sixty-nine times -- and that capability is variadic ports, the same gap the engine spells AddOptionPin. One new proof, unreal_material_editor_matertial_paste_here: Fragment stores every node relative to the selection's centroid, so insert(at) places the FRAGMENT, a distinction one node cannot show and three can. Counterfactuals 12/12 caught, and CF-6 earned its keep twice -- it first PASSED against a no-op edit, and fixing the edit to genuinely forbid a newline in the base clause showed the scope check could not see a class the parser stops recognising, because its input is the parser's own output; a second, deliberately dumber reading of the base clause is now the audit. Registers debt-census-stops-at-engine-source-editor: 559 commands in 49 classes across 27 Engine/Plugins modules that declare their own graph schema (Niagara, MetaSound, PCG, RigVM, ControlRig, StateTree, Optimus) are outside the scope, the tool prints that number every run, and the key must carry the module before the denominator grows because visual script editor commands and FEditorCommands each exist twice

the geometry of a byte dump is a value: pinion_core::widgets::hex_dump lifts the hex/ascii layout out of hello-hex-dump, which is the analyzer-tool audit's plane-A gap -- the detail tree (row_dissect) was already a crate and the DUMP was not, so an application wanting one had to COPY 1,477 lines, and copying a geometry is a fork because the invariants go with it and then drift. Declared `none` rather than `dcc`: this axis's three named families are property grid, data grid and node graph, and a hex dump is none of them, so crediting it would inflate an axis for work it is not named for (R1542's lesson). What makes it worth a type is that a byte appears in TWO disjoint places -- its two hex digits and its one ascii glyph -- so a dump needs byte->cell to paint and cell->byte to hit-test and the two must not be able to disagree. Before this they were three hand-written functions that agreed by inspection, beside FIVE hand-computed column constants (ASCII_BAR_L 60, ASCII_START 61, ASCII_BAR_R 77, TOTAL_COLS 78, HEX_START 10) a person had derived once on paper from a 16-byte row split into two groups of 8; widen the row and every one of them is wrong with nothing to say so. HexLayout is the declaration and every column is derived from it, region_at is the ONLY place a cell is read, and a round-trip property over eight layouts -- including a group that does not divide the row, a row narrower than a group, and a short final row -- is what keeps the forward map and the inverse together. The test that the derivations reproduce all five paper constants exactly is what proves the lift faithful rather than merely compiling. Two things past what a hex view normally does: a cell that is not a byte says WHAT it is (Region names the offset field, the gutter bars and the padding apart, where the old hit-test answered Option<usize> so "you clicked the offset column" and "you clicked a group gap" were one value), and a hex cell names its NIBBLE, which is the difference between overtyping one digit and overtyping the byte -- the thing a hex editor is for. THE MIGRATION CAUGHT A WIRE CHANGE I HAD MADE WITHOUT MEANING TO: ByteSelection::hex defaulted to space-separated pairs and the existing consumer's contract was "0000002c" with no separator, so the example's own tests went red. The separator is now the caller's, and that is the honest resolution rather than a default -- a clipboard payload and a status readout want different ones, and a crate picking one makes a presentation decision for every consumer. Also confirmed the class this project keeps paying for: cargo check compiles the bin and NOT the test target, so the stale constants in the example's tests were invisible until the tests ran. 14 crate tests, 22 example tests, the R1400 demo re-passing unchanged as the proof the migration preserved the wire, 5/5 counterfactuals caught

a dashboard's tiles are a value, and the layout it needs already existed: pinion_core::widgets::tile_grid. THE FINDING IS WHAT THIS ROUND DID NOT BUILD. The tile-dashboard debt asked for one thing first -- measure whether R1560's CSS Grid already holds a dashboard of the class a monitoring tool draws before adding a second layout kind -- and pinion-runtime's tile_dashboard_measurement now answers it as a TEST rather than a paragraph: a full-width header, two halves and a two-row-tall card on twelve Fr(1.0) tracks resolve to the exact pixels a 12-column dashboard wants, and widening one card leaves the other rows' columns alone, which is the property a splitter tree cannot have because grid tracks are sized once ACROSS the container. So no new layout was written. What was missing is the half a layout engine has no opinion about: which tile is where, the rule that keeps two off one slot, and what a drag does to the tiles it lands on. TileGrid holds tiles that do not overlap and every operation keeps that true or is refused by name; the difficulty is not rejection but a reflow that terminates and is deterministic, and both properties come from one rule -- a displaced tile only ever moves DOWN, to just below the lowest tile it collided with, so rows increase monotonically over a finite set. Two things past the dashboard tool, which pushes panels silently as a side effect of the drag: a move REPORTS what it displaced (Reflow names every tile and the row it came from, which is what an undo record and an agent driving the board both need), and compaction is a VERB rather than a consequence, because floating tiles up automatically gives a drag a non-local effect nobody asked for and makes its inverse not a drag. A counterfactual-grade finding came from a failing test the implementation won: the first draft expected a drag to displace a tile in a column it does not share, and the reflow correctly left it alone -- the effect is LOCAL, which is the thing the doc claims and now the thing a test asserts. DELIBERATE INCOMPLETENESS, NAMED: there is no consumer and therefore no demo, so the round breaks the standing visible-deliverable obligation rather than quietly satisfying it with a unit test. The debt keeps its gesture axis open; wiring a pointer drag and an RPC verb to move_to / resize / compact is the next slice and it is what actually closes it. 13 model tests, 2 layout measurements, 6/6 counterfactuals caught

the tile dashboard gets its gesture, and the model's claim gets a cursor: examples/hello-tile-dashboard plus tools/demos/r1608_tile_dashboard.py close the axis R1607 deliberately left open, and R1607 said in its own changelog that a consumer was the only thing that could tell us whether the reflow's LOCALITY holds under a real pointer. It does. Three layers meet here and only one is new -- the layout is R1560's CSS Grid, the arrangement is R1607's TileGrid, and the gesture is this file: a press latches the card under the cursor AND the cell the grab happened at relative to that card, each move snaps the cursor to a cell and subtracts the grab offset, the release lets go. THE GRAB OFFSET IS THE WHOLE TRICK: snapping the cursor's cell and moving the card's top-left there makes a card jump under the pointer the moment it is grabbed anywhere but its corner, which is the difference between a drag and a teleport. The model cannot be WidgetCore::State because State is Copy and an arrangement is a Vec, so the state lives in an Owner::cache'd signal the oracle and the view SHARE -- hello-node-groups' shape -- which also means the painter and the wire read one arrangement rather than two copies that could disagree. Every gesture is a verb over the wire (move_to / resize / compact / remove) and the whole board is one JSON read (layout), so an agent rearranges it with no pixel; every slot is read-only and a read-only refusal is told apart from an unknown path, which is R1566's rule rather than this binding's invention. Past the dashboard tool on the wire too: last_reflow names what a gesture displaced INCLUDING the transitive case, a card pushed by a card that was itself pushed. FOUR OF THE ROUND'S ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT EACH TIME, which is the round's real content: `alarms` at eight columns wide cannot move in a grid of twelve, so the drag fixture had to be a narrower card (the clamp was correct); the displacement list was longer than expected because the reflow is transitive; a 6x2 resize came out clean because the rows it grew into were empty by then; and a card sharing no column with the dragged one is not touched at all. That last one is the locality the model's doc claimed and the demo now asserts over the wire. 13 example tests, a demo with 40 assertions over ten sections, and the painted board read out of scene/snapshot rather than assumed

a tile board is editable without a pointer, and an edge is a HANDLE: closes both axes of debt-tile-board-gesture-surface-incomplete, the debt R1608's own close audit registered. Declared `none` on R1606/R1607/R1608's precedent -- this axis's three named families are property grid, data grid and node graph, and a dashboard shell is none of them, so crediting a round to it would inflate an axis for work it is not named for. The two axes close TOGETHER because they are one derivation: set_edge puts one side of a card on a grid line and holds the opposite side still, and a handle drag calls it once per edge while a Grow/Shrink chord calls it once with a one-cell step. The toolkit's floor here is real -- MDI child window has keyboard move AND resize -- and five things are chosen differently, each measured against the toolkit's widget module 6.11.1 rather than assumed. NO MODE: the toolkit's keyboard editing lives behind isInInteractiveMode, entered only from the system menu (_q_enterInteractiveMode casts q->sender() to a action and returns unless it is MoveAction or ResizeAction), so one arrow key means different things depending on state the user cannot see; TileNudge is twelve flat values and the chord says which. NOTHING WARPS THE POINTER: the toolkit computes each arrow as mapFromGlobal(cursor().pos() + delta) and then cursor().setPos(...), with the whole keyPressEvent body inside #ifndef QT_NO_CURSOR, so a cursor-less build has no keyboard layout editing at all and every other build jumps the physical mouse. AN EDIT CAN BE TAKEN BACK: the toolkit stores oldGeometry on entering interactive mode and never reads it, since Key_Escape, Key_Return and Key_Enter all fall to one leaveInteractiveMode() -- and even restoring the rectangle would not be enough, because a move displaces OTHER cards, which is why TileEdit holds the whole arrangement and Escape restores the board. A SESSION'S REFLOW IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A SUM: four chords that walk a card down past another push it once, 1>5, where summing the per-chord reflows reports four displacements of a card that moved a single time; Reflow::between derives it from the two arrangements. ARROW NAVIGATION IS TOTAL, AND THE INVARIANT IS WHY: negate Tile::overlaps and what is left is exactly "separated on some axis in some direction", so every other card lies beyond one of the four edges and TileGrid::neighbour can reach all of them -- MDI area cannot make that claim because its subwindows may overlap, which is why its navigation is activateNextSubWindow, a walk down a list in creation order. On the pointer side, the toolkit's initOperationMap hand-writes nine rows pairing a private Operation with a ChangeFlag mask and a cursor, and the enum, the map and the regions are all private, so no caller can enumerate a subwindow's handles; TileHandle::ALL is the enumeration and both the edges it moves and the cursor it asks for are DERIVED, the diagonal's slope included (two start edges or two end edges lie on the nwse diagonal, one of each on nesw). That derivation is what forced CursorHint's two diagonal arms, and the finding there is the debt-window-has-no-level-declaration shape a third time: the R1189 window-chrome path has mapped ResizeDirection::NorthWest to CursorIcon::NwseResize for ~420 rounds, so the capability was proven in-tree and only the scene-node VOCABULARY could not say it. THE ANNOUNCEMENT NEEDED A NEW CHANNEL and it is a framework addition with this board as its forcing consumer: pinion-a11y gains AccessLive (WAI-ARIA aria-live, three arms to accesskit's Live) because the cards an edit displaces are by definition not the one the user is on, so no per-card value can carry the fact. The toolkit 6.8 added accessible announcement event and measured over the toolkit's widget module, NO WIDGET FIRES ONE -- the only references outside qaccessible.{h,cpp} are the platform adapters that deliver it and qtestaccessible.h, and qmdisubwindow.cpp, qmdiarea.cpp and qsizegrip.cpp contain no accessibility notification of any kind, so a toolkit MDI window that moves is silent to a screen reader even though state() advertises movable and sizeable. A DECLARED region rather than a fired event is also the only shape SS2 #7 can report: an event leaves no trace, so scene/access could not publish it and a test could only see it by intercepting a callback. THREE OF THE ROUND'S ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT, which is where its content is. A Grow then a Shrink restores the CARD and not the BOARD, because the reflow only moves tiles down and floating them home is compact's separate verb -- so an inverse gesture is not an undo, which is the argument for TileEdit stated as a test instead of a paragraph. The corner test's first fixture grew both axes and its two routes agreed, because a rectangle reached by two outward steps contains every intermediate; the hazard needs one edge going each way. And the SECOND draft, one such fixture, was caught by a counterfactual -- the more valuable finding, because a per-edge implementation resolves the edges in some fixed order and for any single fixture one of the two orders is harmless, so a fixture where vertical-first is the harmful one let the rejected design pass while the loop takes the horizontal edge first. Both mirror images are therefore fixtures, so no order is safe in both and the assertion is about the DESIGN rather than about one arrangement. And the difference-not-a-sum fixture first walked its card UP, which collides once, so it measured 1 against 1 and could not tell the two answers apart. A FOURTH defect was found by a test rather than by reasoning and it is an interaction one: handles are painted only on the selected card and the first draft hit-tested them on EVERY card, so a press near any card's edge resized it with nothing on screen saying it would. The paint and the gesture now read one fact. Also cleared inline: this tool reported hello-tile-dashboard UNCLASSIFIED for a round, the R1575 / R1577 shape a third time, and it is filed under dcc because dock- is -- a tile board and a dock are two shells that arrange panels. 25 crate tests, 26 example tests, 1 a11y lowering test asserting the accesskit value rather than smoke-testing it, a demo with 76 assertions over thirteen sections, and R1608's demo re-passing unchanged as the proof the wire was preserved

a window declares its LEVEL, and says what became of it: WindowSpec::level plus pinion_core::window_level closes debt-window-has-no-level-declaration, the last open analyzer-tool debt -- plane C asks for a torn-off readout that stays above the application being watched, and the CAPABILITY was already proven in-tree because the shell's drag-preview window has hard-coded an always-on-top level since R1147. Only the vocabulary was missing, which is the shape R1609 had just met for the third time in CursorHint. Declared osnative on R1576's precedent: this is the same WindowSpec axis, and what that axis is gated on is Mac and Windows NATIVE SURFACES, which a window-manager stacking request buildable and testable on Linux is not. THE SHAPE IS CHOSEN AGAINST THE CONVENTIONAL DESKTOP-TOOLKIT ENCODING IN FIVE PLACES, each read from a reference implementation rather than assumed, and each recorded without naming it because a pushed artifact carries the reasoning and not the citation. A LEVEL IS ONE VALUE: the usual encoding is two independent bits in a window-flags word, so on-top-AND-on-bottom is a value a program can build, and three platform backends resolve it three DIFFERENT ways -- one sets both stacking hints on a mapped window while its show path takes only the first match, so the pair means one thing at map time and another on a live change; one warns and picks top; and one never reads the bottom bit at all. THE OUTCOME IS PUBLISHED: a flags accessor returns what the program STORED, so on that third backend a program sets stay-below, reads it back as set, and is wrong -- and it is not a missing platform capability, since the same platform has levels below normal and our window backend drives one. LevelOutcome names applied / unsupported / unknown against the backend actually running, read from the live event loop rather than from a build target because one Linux binary runs on either of the two whose support differs. THE ERROR DIRECTION IS CHOSEN: the table is a MODEL of the window backend and can go stale, so it is arranged to fail as over-reported unsupported, the direction that self-corrects, never as a claimed applied, which is the silent lie above (R1602's asymmetry). CHANGING IT COSTS ONE CALL: a flags-word encoding reparents and hides the window, and on one backend destroys and recreates it, where set_window_level applies live -- which is why the axis has to be reconcilable, a level being a thing the USER toggles. AND THE LEVELS ARE ENUMERABLE: WindowLevel::ALL and the wire's level_names make a level picker buildable from the wire, where two bits in a flags word of twenty unrelated hints carry no enumeration of themselves. TWO LIFTS THE ROUND WAS FORCED INTO RATHER THAN CHOSE. window_axis_changes: the level pass would have been the THIRD hand-written copy of the same same-id walk beside title (R1319) and decorations (R1320), which is the R727/R732 third-consumer mandate exactly, so the three are now one derivation with a projection and window_placement_moves is deliberately NOT expressed through it (a resolution against the live topology is not a field comparison). scene/window_declare: scene/windows published five axes and exactly ONE (position) could be written back, so adding a per-field scene/window_level would have been the second step toward one method per field; the read is one method over the whole declaration and now the write is too, with scene/window_move re-expressed as the position-only patch it always was so two closures cannot give one axis two meanings. Absent / null / a value are three messages, which is what makes going BACK to a WM-placed window expressible at all. INLINE CLEARANCE, AND THE ROUND'S SECOND FINDING: publishing NoAxisDeclared was impossible without touching R1566's vocabulary gate, and the gate turned out to see TWO of the FOUR shapes this dispatcher emits a word in. Eighteen words reached the wire that a client could only learn by reading pinion's source -- ClosureUnavailable, InputInjectionUnavailable from 24 call sites, InvalidSize, OutOfBounds, SnapshotFailed and the rest -- inside the gate built to make that impossible. The scan now walks the let-variant-match blocks STRUCTURALLY, which a line-local rule cannot do because the arrow-quote-Word spelling is also how a dozen VALUE enums write their wire names (measured: sixteen collected as refusals), and correctly excludes apply_error_to_rpc, which shares the shape and builds an OBJECT payload. Vocabulary 17 -> 35 with no new refusal written. R1605's lesson a second time: make every emission account for itself rather than finding the ones you know how to find

the reference-name directive gets a gate, and the framework crates get cleared: tools/reference_names.py counts every occurrence of another project's name in a tracked file and refuses a push that raises it, file by file. THE GATE IS THE POINT. The directive arrived at the end of R1610, which zeroed its own output and registered the rest as debt -- and nothing measured the rest, so nobody could see it was 7,999 occurrences across 501 files. A directive whose state is invisible grows. THE RECORDED PRESCRIPTION DID NOT SURVIVE THE MEASUREMENT: R1610 wrote 'restate every sentence by hand', which at 7,999 is a wish rather than a plan, and this is R1571's lesson again -- a prescription is a hypothesis until someone implements it. What replaces it is a DERIVED substitution: a toolkit class name is its own generic noun with a letter in front, so the capability claim the sentence carries survives whole and only the vendor leaves. FIVE DEFECTS IN THE MIGRATOR WERE FOUND BY GATES AND TESTS RATHER THAN BY READING, which is where the round's content is. Its own selftest caught an abbreviation's full stop read as a sentence end, and then the inner-doc marker's own exclamation mark read the same way. The doc gate caught a URL rewritten inside its host name and link-reference definitions joined into one line by the re-flow. Clippy caught a code span's opening backtick eaten when the closing one was not adjacent. And the doc gate caught a re-flow splitting a code span across lines, which made the following bullet read as its continuation. THE RATCHET CAUGHT ITS OWN AUTHOR: the new hook tests needed fixture names, so the gate refused the commit that added them -- the fixtures now assemble their strings from pieces, because an exemption for the test of a detector is the loophole every detector dies of. Negative controls for both refusal shapes. crates/ 3,662 -> 436 and examples/ 912 -> 110, with fmt, workspace clippy, cargo doc and the doctests green; tools/ 1,548 and docs/ 1,844 remain and are budgeted rather than forgotten, the largest block of them being the capability census, whose ids are DATA and need a design rather than an edit. Two exclusions are structural and say so: the decision ledger cannot be amended after it is frozen, and vendored character data is not our prose. 113 hook assertions, 24 migrator cases, 14 classifier cases

the census stops naming the vendor, and the sweep reaches the prose a line-local rule could not see: 7,999 -> 687, which is 91 percent of the population R1611 measured. THE CENSUS WAS THE HARD THIRD, and the design answer is a RENAME rather than an encoding. An operator id is a vendor prefix followed by a capability, and the capability half is already the generic name -- add_group IS add group -- so stripping the prefix removes the identity and loses nothing a maintainer needs. Hashing the ids was the other option and it would have made a 3,600-line proof table unreadable to the people who keep it. An owner becomes exactly the stem proof_name already derived from it, which is why every proof identifier in the crates kept the name it had; the where field, 197 occurrences of a reference tree's directory layout, is provenance for a local audit and is now regenerated rather than committed. The generator learned the same spelling so a regeneration cannot undo the round, with four selftest cases holding it there, and the generator itself is the one file excluded on the ground that reading a tree requires knowing its layout. THREE DEFECTS FOUND BY GATES, NOT BY READING. A blunt word rewrite renamed a LOCAL VARIABLE, and the compiler caught it. The bijection test caught a second proof file the sweep had missed entirely, naming the exact three rows that disagreed. And the round's own repair pass was computing the fix and throwing it away, because the write was gated on a name having been found in the file -- a file whose names were already gone still carried the double article an earlier pass left. TWO GRAMMAR RULES WERE WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: no was missing from the determiner set, so 'no comparison surfaces this' became 'no the comparison'; and that was PRESENT in it, so 'three things that it cannot answer' would have lost the article it needs. The prose mask is the other half: the demos carry their explanation in the module docstring, not in # comments, so 1,107 occurrences were invisible to a line-local rule -- only the module docstring counts, because a later triple-quoted string may be a payload an assertion compares against. Products whose lowercase form is ordinary English are counted capitalised only, and Sketch is left out with the reason written down. fmt, workspace clippy, cargo doc, the doctests and 3,500 crate tests green; 687 remain as a long tail of individual sentences, no file holding more than 31. R1612.1 -- the round audits its own detector and finds it blind: the engine symbol patterns listed whole CLASS names, so a source FILE name went uncounted because a file name drops the leading type letter, and a compiler class went uncounted because an underscore ends `[A-Za-z]*`. Counting on doubt means the STEM is the pattern, not the class. Widening it surfaced 215 occurrences the ratchet had been passing, one subsystem owner among them, which is now renamed the same derived way as the rest with the generator taught to agree. Also removed the four trims in proof_name that stripped a vendor class prefix: the owner now arrives already reduced to that stem, so they were dead code AND the last spelling of that prefix in a published file, short enough that the census did not recognise them. The bijection test passing with them gone is the proof they were dead. AND THE RATCHET REFUSED THIS ROW'S FIRST DRAFT, which quoted the two symbols it was reporting on -- the second time in two rounds that the gate caught its own author, and the reason a detector's own paperwork gets no exemption. 766 remain, honestly counted. R1612.3 -- STOP-THE-LINE: the push gate refused, because the base's last CI run was red, and the red was R1610's. Its wire census had been taught that a three-state patch is legitimately BOTH absent-able and null-able, and the demo that reads the published schema had not -- so the invariant 'either flag, never both' held for every field until the first patch was published, and it went red in the full sweep, which runs only in CI. THE FIX IS THAT THE WIRE SAYS IT: WireField gains `patch`, and the rule becomes a BICONDITIONAL -- both flags iff a patch -- which catches the mistake in both directions where the prohibition caught one. A client reading both flags could not otherwise tell a deliberate three-state patch from a key declared two contradictory ways. Same shape as R1610's own second finding and R1611's fourth: a gate that knows one of the emission shapes is not a gate, and this project now has three recorded instances of TWO READERS of one census disagreeing after only one was taught

a byte dump paints from the map that hit-tests it: pinion_widget_paint::hex_dump::view_hex_dump closes the analyzer-tool audit's LAST plane-A gap, the asymmetry R1606 left behind -- the detail tree's paint was already a crate (view_virtual_tree) and the dump's was 55 lines inside the example, so an application depending on one got a picture and depending on the other got a map and homework. Declared `none` rather than `dcc` for the same reason R1606 was: this axis's three named families are property grid, data grid and node graph, and a hex dump is none of them, so crediting it would inflate an axis for work it is not named for. THE MOVE IS NOT A RELOCATION. The painter asks region_at what each cell IS and glyph_at what it SHOWS, which are the two questions a pointer asks, so what is drawn and what responds are one fact -- the general form of debt-paint-and-gesture-read-two-facts, demonstrated. That forced region_at to become closed form: a scan of the row is fine for one pointer and quadratic for a painter that asks about every cell, and the closed form is held to the scan it replaced by an exhaustive property. THE OFFSET COLUMN WAS BROKEN AND NOBODY COULD SEE IT: the example formatted the row offset to a fixed eight hex digits and then TRUNCATED to offset_digits, so every width below eight printed the leading zeros of an eight-digit number -- 0000 on every row -- and the declaration's own width was the one thing never exercised. glyph_at derives the digit instead. MARKS ARE NAMED, NOT COLOURED: MarkSet is a declaration-ordered list of named byte runs with no colour, names_at(byte) answers WHY a byte is lit with the stack that decided it, and overlap resolves LAST-wins for every visual channel alike. The reference for that is a mature toolkit's range-decoration list over a text layout, and the difference is the point: there a decoration is (start, length, format) so the run has no identity apart from how it looks, and the draw loop resolves background last-wins while suppressing a later foreground wherever an earlier one already drew -- two directions in one list, documented nowhere and queryable not at all. 13 counterfactuals, 13 caught, and ONE PASSED FIRST: the paint crate had restated the printable-byte rule the geometry already owned, and narrowing it to drop the space broke nothing because no fixture held a space. The fix was not a better fixture but deleting the second copy -- the painter now asks whether the glyph IS the byte, which cannot drift from a rule it does not restate. CellRole exists so a new Region cannot go unpainted: Region stays non_exhaustive for the hit-test, role() collapses it inside the crate where the match is exhaustive, and CellRole is deliberately NOT non_exhaustive so a new role breaks every painter loudly rather than falling into a wildcard.

the reference names reach zero, and the last ones left say why they stay: 7,999 -> 766 was R1611 and R1612's work, and this round takes 766 -> 0 by teaching the migration tool the three things it had deliberately reported and left alone. THE ID FAMILIES ARE DERIVATIONS TOO, which is what the first pass had not seen: an operator id is <vendor prefix>_<capability> so the capability is what is left when the prefix goes -- and it is the SAME spelling reference_census.py's public_id already derives, so prose and proof tables agree by construction rather than by care; a C struct is `b` + its own generic noun exactly as a toolkit class is `Q` + one; an engine class is <type-prefix><subsystem><Rest> where the subsystem word is the vendor's spelling of a generic thing -- a graph, a node in the visual-script graph, that language's compiler, a visual script. A DOC LINK IS REMOVED, NOT REWORDED: the first pass refused any line holding a URL and was right to (substituting inside a host produced doc.the-toolkit.io), but refusing it left the citation, so the definition line goes whole, the label it defined loses its brackets so no rustdoc link dangles, and the name inside is then an ordinary symbol. Only a TRAILING blank comment is dropped with it -- the blank before a SURVIVING definition is load-bearing, because a link reference glued to the paragraph above stops being a definition, which is how that rule was found: two broken rustdoc links at the gate. THE REMAINING POPULATION WAS ASSERTION LABELS, and the answer is not a cleverer classifier but a JUDGE: --in-strings is opt-in per file, a rewritten payload fails its own test and a rewritten demo string fails its own demo. It caught its own error immediately -- a local variable abbreviating a quit sink collided with a product name and became `let the toolkit =`, and the compiler said so. THE WRAPPER WAS MEASURING THE WRONG LINE: the code-span placeholder was three characters standing in for eighteen, so every re-flowed paragraph holding a span came out over the margin by the difference, and nothing failed because no lint measures a comment -- the only witness is a reader, and the first pass had none. AND ZERO IS NOT ZERO EVERYWHERE: the design-parity workflow's host name, token header and environment variable are an ADDRESS rather than a citation, so everything that was ours to name was renamed to its role (pinion design-verify / design-fetch-image / design-diff, design_* modules, examples/design-button-m3) and the three constants were gathered into crates/pinion-cli/src/design_api.rs so the exclusion could be that one file. The prose around it stays counted, so a citation cannot regrow behind the exclusion. .gitignore is excluded for the same shape of reason: an ignore pattern IS the directory an editor creates. Declared `none` rather than an axis: this is a standing-directive clearance, and no Phase B capability moved. R1614.1 -- the census reads its own pin again. R1612 renamed the pin's tree names and operator ids to their public spelling and taught `emit` to write them that way; it did not teach `report` to READ them that way, so the lookup missed on every run. The consequence was silent in the worst direction: coverage printed nothing at all because the denominator was zero, and all 679 judged operators were listed as unmeasured, while --check-pin -- which reads the pin directly and never touches a live tree -- went on reporting 679 judged and 0 problems. TWO READERS OF ONE CENSUS, ONE TAUGHT: the same shape as R1612.3's wire census, this time inside the tool that recorded the class. THE NUMBERS ARE BACK AND THEY MOVED: the DCC is 54/76 = 71 percent where the last audit recorded 54/72 = 75, so four operators appeared in the reference and the denominator grew while the numerator did not; the engine is 85/211 = 40, unchanged in rate; 301 live operators are unjudged, which is the real state the node-coverage campaign works against. AND THE ROUND'S FIRST TEST WAS THE WRONG TEST: it asserted the PIN's shape, and a counterfactual restoring the broken lookup PASSED it, because the artifact was never what broke. Replaced with one that runs report over a synthetic tree and pin; both halves of the fix now have a counterfactual that catches them.

the scene says WHY it painted, and a run says what it IS: pinion_core::marks plus StyleRun::name plus scene/marks closes debt-scene-cannot-say-which-marks-it-painted, the analyzer-tool plane-A debt R1613's own close audit opened. Declared `text` because the general consumer is the styled-run substrate: a StyleRun is the framework's FormatRange, and this round is what gives one an identity. THE DEFECT IS NOT A HEX-DUMP DEFECT. R1613 put the dump's marks_at oracle on the binding that owns the drag selection, so the brush window -- which belongs to a SIBLING external -- had to be fetched by the client and handed back in as an argument. The client was reassembling, on its own side, a composition the view had already performed and then discarded. Whenever a widget's appearance is decided by more than one external, the composed fact belongs to no single oracle, and the view is the only place that can publish it. THE CENSUS THE DEBT DEMANDED, MEASURED NOT ESTIMATED (tools/assembled_state.py): 73 multi-external bindings, 11 of which read more than one external, 1 of which publishes the assembly. Its own selftest caught the scan short twice -- the direct find_external_with_tag form misses hello-hex-dump entirely, which reads its brush through a typed reader one crate over, and the check that the typed-reader list is not short first answered 5 by counting four rustdoc mentions and a free function. Unresolvable tag arguments are REPORTED, 16 bindings of them, rather than dropped. A SECOND CONSUMER, AND IT IS THE LEGIBLE ONE: highlight_code has always classified a token as keyword / string / comment / number and then kept only a colour -- and the colour is not even a stable name for the class, because the light and dark schemes paint the same class two different inks. A run now names its class, so the ink and the reason for it are ONE declaration that cannot drift. PAST THE REFERENCE IN THREE PLACES, each read from the reference source rather than assumed: its range decoration IS its format, so two runs resolving to the same ink are indistinguishable once drawn (a name can be smuggled through the format type's open integer-keyed property space, but nothing declares one); the list is handed over whole, so which-runs-cover-offset-N is every caller's own loop; and the runs are always over characters, where a dump's are over BYTES of the inspected buffer and the cells showing them are three times as many, which is why a MarkSet has no domain-less constructor. FOUR OUTCOMES, NOT TWO: published / silent / no-channel / no-such-tag, and the no-channel arm carries WHICH kind of nothing -- uniform, structural or opaque -- so an agent learns from the wire that a Box has nothing to attribute rather than that a widget forgot to. SceneNodeKind::marks_channel is exhaustive so a node kind added later must say which it is. THREE FINDINGS FROM 20 COUNTERFACTUALS. The census test compared the declaration to the declaration, so retagging Container as Opaque passed; the expected channel is now DERIVED from behaviour three other matches already implement (does find_with_tag descend it, does find_external_with_tag resolve it, does it carry a tag at all). Nothing asserted that the field's text node carries field_text_tag, so deleting the tag left the whole Rust suite green with only a demo to notice. And Some(empty) versus None on TextGridNode::marks -- a terminal that never attributes its cells against a dump with nothing selected this frame -- was documented as two facts and tested only one layer up, on MarksLookup, which is not the layer that can get it wrong. A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND BY A DEMO AND IS NOW UNIT-GATED: tagging the field's text node made it a candidate hit-target for the input router, and every interior click stopped positioning the caret -- the current-line band's own comment had predicted it, saying it works today only because the untagged text node shadows it. Inline clearance: the -32602 vocabulary gate recognised the Word-colon-detail shape by two hard-coded call-site names, so R1615's UnknownTag would have been reported dead and UnknownProposalKind had been on the wire unpublished since it was written; the rule is derived from the shape now. 20 counterfactuals, 20 caught after repair; a 45-assertion demo on the code editor, R1613's demo re-passing through the new wire as proof the question got smaller, and 19 field-bearing demos re-run for the router regression.

the wire says what a level MAY be: WireField.values plus window_declare::LEVEL_WIRE_NAMES closes debt-window-level-vocabulary-not-on-the-framework-wire, the analyzer-tool plane-C debt R1610.1's own close audit opened. Declared `api` because the deliverable is a SCHEMA capability -- a key with a closed value set now says so and says which values -- rather than a window capability; R1610 already took osnative for the level itself. THE DEFECT IS R1566's, ONE FIELD OVER. R1610.1 projected the level onto a String for two good reasons -- this crate owns the wire shape, and the axis must be parsed BEFORE any other axis in the same message is applied rather than aborting the whole frame at deserialization -- and its own carry named the cost: the earlier Option<WindowLevel> draft got serde's unknown-variant error, which LISTS the valid values, and the projection threw that away. What was left was UnknownLevel, a word telling a client its spelling was wrong and never what a right one looks like, plus level_names on one binding's own external, which is an application surface another binding need not have. Knowing that matching is safe is worthless without knowing what to match -- the exact thing R1566 fixed for error payloads, and the gate R1610 repaired while reintroducing the shape beside it. VALUES IS THE VALUE HALF OF OF, NOT A SECOND SPELLING OF IT. `of` names a censused TYPE and only a typed Rust field can carry one, because the census compares its declaration against the parsed source; a key deliberately typed String therefore has no way to reference an enum, and the closed set it accepts had nowhere to live. WireField.values is that slot, and the census describes its own new key so an agent reading rpc/schema learns the slot exists the same way it learns every other. THE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER RETYPED: LEVEL_WIRE_NAMES is a const computed in a while loop from WindowLevel::ALL, so its length is the domain census's length by construction and there is no second copy of a closed set to go stale in silence. A hand list here would have been the debt's own shape one layer down. THE PUBLISHED SET AND THE ACCEPTED SET ARE PROVEN TO BE ONE SET, which is the only thing that makes publishing worth anything: every published spelling is driven through the real window_declare parse path and must land, and a non-member must be refused by name, with the negative control asserting it is genuinely outside the set. That check lives with the axis because only the axis knows its parse path; what is general lives in the census gate -- a values declaration must sit on a string-bearing key, be non-empty, and hold distinct non-empty spellings, and at least one field must declare one, because a census slot nothing fills is a promise to a client nobody keeps. AND THE REFUSAL NOW LEADS SOMEWHERE: the -32602 entry says that a word naming a closed value set does not carry the set and that rpc/schema does, by the name of the slot. A word that leads to pinion's source is the loop this whole surface exists to end. 5 counterfactuals, 5 caught after one was found to be MISWRITTEN rather than uncaught -- it deleted the tail of the sentence and left the pointer intact, so the gate was right and the counterfactual was wrong, which is worth recording because a PASSED counterfactual is normally a finding and this one was a fixture defect. A 40-assertion demo reads the value set off rpc/schema, drives every published spelling, refuses four non-members, and round-trips a value read from scene/windows straight back into scene/window_declare -- the read and write sides speaking one vocabulary. r1610, r1576, r1539 and r1089 re-pass unchanged.

a window says WHOSE answer it is: pinion_core::display::DisplayHome plus scene/windows.display_home plus use_window_home close debt-display-home-not-cross-checked, and crates/pinion-shell/tests/winit_level_model.rs closes debt-level-support-models-a-vendored-crate -- the analyzer-tool audit's two remaining plane-C debts, both registered by R1576 and R1610's own close audits. Declared osnative because both are window-system integration, and the tool DEMANDED a re-judgment of this axis (round-axis 1 -> 3), which is recorded as 63 -> 66 below. THE DEFECT WAS A DERIVATION NOBODY CHECKED. R1576 derives a window's home from its rectangle -- the display with the largest share -- and deliberately keeps no second stored copy. The window system HAS a second answer and we never once compared them, so a divergence was not a fact this framework could hold. Measured against the window backend's own four desktop implementations rather than assumed, there are FOUR RULES: two resolve by largest intersection, one caches an answer refreshed only inside a synthetic configure path when the scale factor changes, and one reports the first compositor output the surface entered, which is not geometric at all -- and one of them answers with the FIRST ENUMERATED monitor for a window that is on no monitor, where this framework answers nowhere. So the two can differ without either being wrong, which is why this is a REPORT and not a gate: a gate would have to invent a rule overriding a platform's own. DisplayHome is five arms over the product of two options, its single constructor is the only way to build one, and its published vocabulary is proved by DRIVING that constructor over every combination and asserting set equality -- a stronger claim than a const derived from a data-less enum can make, because it pins what the code can emit rather than what the type declares. PAST THE TOOLKIT BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY ASSERTION: it has both answers too and HIDES ONE. Its geometric resolver is declared in a private header so an application cannot call it, it decides by CENTRE POINT (a window nine tenths on the right panel whose centre is on the left resolves left) with a fallback that keeps the LAST intersecting sibling it iterated, and it is consulted only when the application itself moves the window -- and even then short-circuits whenever the current screen contains the centre. A user dragging across a seam never runs it. Nothing there puts the two side by side and an application cannot, because one of them is unreachable; the public screen-at query takes a POINT, which is the rectangle-shaped gap R1576 already recorded. THE MODEL OF A VENDORED CRATE IS NOW CHECKED AGAINST IT. R1610 wrote the per-backend level table by reading the backend's source once; nothing held the two together, so the backend implementing Wayland stacking would leave our table saying unsupported forever with neither compiler nor test noticing. The gate parses every set_window_level under platform_impl with a real parser (not a regex -- R1527) and classifies each from TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS that must agree: the parameter binding is underscore-prefixed, and its identifier does not occur in the body. When they disagree it FAILS rather than guesses. The claim is therefore exact in one direction and bounded in the other, which is stated rather than papered over: every Unsupported verdict is proved to be a deliberate no-op, every Applied verdict only that the level reaches the implementation. The census is keyed by PATH and an unrecognised one fails, because a version bump that moves or adds a backend is exactly when the model needs re-reading. It also states the under-report it is making on purpose: one unnamed backend genuinely drives levels and we report Unknown for it. THE BINDING GETS THE SAME READ, because a window's screen accessor is ordinary application API in the toolkit and leaving in-process code below that while the wire is past it is the wrong asymmetry (R1576's own argument). One derivation, two callers: the view uses the hook, the oracle uses the handle it resolved at wiring time, and both funnel into one formatter. THE STAMP HAD TO MOVE TOO -- homes are stamped at window creation and on every Moved, not only at RPC dispatch, because a GUI-only session issues no dispatch and the painted readout would have shown where the window was at boot, forever. Cost checked against the backend rather than assumed: its monitor enumeration is cached behind a lock, leaving one outer-position read per window, which is what the cursor path already pays. R1616's values slot gains four more consumers: level_outcome's kind, declared and backend all carry closed sets and R1610 published none of them. 17 COUNTERFACTUALS, 17 CAUGHT, AND THE ROUND'S THREE REAL FINDINGS CAME FROM THEM. The substrate test could not tell a wholesale replacement from a merge because its only stamp was the first one, so the map was empty either way -- the handle-side twin WAS caught, which is what named the gap. Nothing checked that a published value set is what its producer emits, only that it was well-formed, so the census could retype a closed set by hand and stay green: that is R1616's own second-copy failure reintroduced inside the census, and it now has a test that drives each producer and compares. And the round's scratch driver restored with a metadata-preserving copy, so the restored file looked OLDER than the artifact built from the defect and cargo served that artifact to the next case -- the concrete form of the standing rebuild-after-revert rule, and every verdict after the first restore was void until the whole run was redone. The committed driver (R1600.1) does not have that bug and REFUSES a scoped gate, which is the other mistake the scratch run made; the final run went through it with one unscoped whole-suite gate. A 46-assertion demo, and r1576, r1610 and r1616 re-pass unchanged.

a node that paints from ONE declaration still says why: pinion_core::marks domain::NODE plus MarkSet::whole/because plus marks on Box, Path, Image and Container advance debt-assembled-state-is-published-by-one-binding, the analyzer-tool plane-A debt R1615 registered. Declared `none` because no Phase B capability moved -- this is an introspection channel reaching the nodes it had skipped, and R1615 took the text axis for the mechanism itself. THE DEBT SAID COVERAGE AND IT WAS MECHANISM. Its own file recorded that R1615 closed the mechanism and only coverage remained; measured, the mechanism reached Text and TextGrid alone, and everything the other ten bindings assemble -- a grid row, a selected cell, a dimmed port, a colour pad -- is a filled rectangle whose marks channel is Uniform, which R1615 read as having nothing to attribute. It is the opposite. "The node itself IS the run" was always a statement about the SHAPE of the attribution, not about its absence, and a rectangle's colour is routinely a composition -- selected, and hovered, and inside a collapsed group -- whose parts live in different externals. domain::NODE is that index space: one position, the node. Stated as a domain rather than as a second list on purpose, so the declaration order, the last-wins rule, the positional query and the wire form stay ONE mechanism; a caller writes because(name) and never an index, because a [0, 0) run covers nothing and would publish a reason that answers no question. THE CENSUS WAS COUNTING A DIFFERENT QUESTION, and that is the round's largest finding. The debt asks whether a widget's APPEARANCE is a function of several externals; the tool counted whether a file READS several anywhere in its source. The two come apart in both directions and both were measured: hello-row-dissect reads its second external inside apply_access_action, which runs after the picture and cannot decide it, while hello-grouped-grid and hello-grouped-list read two in read_state and then paint with view(state.selected, frame), dropping one. What makes this decidable rather than a judgment call is STRUCTURAL: WidgetCore::view(state, frame) is handed no &Scene at all, so a view cannot read an external and every path from an external to the picture runs through read_state. Reads are now bucketed by the function body they sit in, with call following to a FIXPOINT rather than one level -- the binding this census exists for reaches its second external through read_state -> read_brush -> brush(), so a one-level scan dropped the subject of the debt out of its own population, which its own selftest then caught. Every read outside that path is REPORTED under the function it sits in rather than dropped, R1605's rule. 11 -> 6, and the whole-file count is printed beside it because the difference IS the finding. A VERDICT IS NOW A THING WITH A PROOF. The debt allowed two answers for an assembling binding -- publish, or record why it need not -- and the second only with proof. Four bindings carry one: the two grouped ones because their roving cursor steers the keyboard and the accessibility tree and is never painted, and hello-selection-toolbar and settings-panel because their assembly is SPATIAL, two widgets side by side rather than one node decided by several. Each proof is behavioural and lives in that binding's own tests -- hold one external still, vary the other, assert the painted subtree is byte-identical, with a negative control asserting the other direction DOES move -- so a binding that starts painting the second contribution fails its own proof and owes the publication. The tool REFUSES a verdict whose named test is absent, and refuses one for a binding that no longer assembles. ASSEMBLE 6, PUBLISH 2, VERDICT 4, OPEN 0, and OPEN 0 is a gate rather than a number somebody reads. THE FORCING CONSUMER IS HONEST: the colour picker's saturation/value pad has its BASE from the hue slider and its THUMB from itself, so it is one painted node that is genuinely a function of two externals, and a client asking why it is that colour previously got half an answer from either and had to compose the other half -- which means reimplementing the framework's composition client-side. It also forced the sharpest design finding: that pad is a CONTAINER, and a container paints its own BoxStyle. Structural's doc claimed such a node "paints nothing of its own", which is false for the commonest shape there is, a panel with a background. So a container publishes the reasons for its own fill while its children carry their own, and the channel keeps describing where the CONTENT's attribution lives. No enum arm was added; a doc that was wrong was corrected. TWO OF R1615's OWN TESTS BECAME FALSE AND WERE REPAIRED WITHOUT LOSING THEIR TEETH: the channel derivation keyed Carries off "this kind answers Silent", which a box now does too, so it keys off WHICH INDEX SPACE the kind publishes in -- read by asking each kind to publish one reason through its own real API, a fourth independent statement that never reads marks_channel. And a plain box is now Silent rather than NoChannel: nobody asked, which stays distinct from having no channel at all. THE GATE CAUGHT THE AUTHOR TWICE. A const declaration inserted between an #[allow] and the fn it applied to silently detached it, and clippy reported the two lints that attribute had been suppressing. The settings-panel proof's first draft asserted on the font slider, which the default section does not paint, so find_with_tag answered None -- the tags were then read out of the painted scene rather than assumed. And the grouped bindings' negative control failed on correct code because source row 3 sits in a collapsed group, so the control now SEARCHES for a selection that moves the picture instead of picking one. 10 counterfactuals through the committed driver under one unscoped gate that runs the Rust suites AND the census's own tests AND the census, because four of them break a tool no cargo test can see. A 33-assertion demo, and r1615, r1613 and r709 re-pass unchanged.

the pointer wire says WHICH BUTTONS ARE HELD: PointerButtons promoted from the raw capture channel to the router's own per-pointer state, stamped onto every dispatched pointer event, closing debt-pointer-wire-omits-held-button-state and with it the Model/View axis's named blocked item, drag-select across sections. Declared `modelview` because that axis recorded the gap by name at R1562 and re-recorded it at R1563; the catalog axis was waiting on the same one item. THE DEBT FILE'S DIAGNOSIS WAS HALF WRONG AND IT COST 188 LINES. It said the type had no counterpart on the wire. The TYPE existed from R1418, lmr codec and all -- what was missing was the CHANNEL: the held set rode RawPointerButton only, which an External reaches by opting into wants_raw_pointer_buttons, so a drag-select gesture (by definition a press that leaves the pressed widget) could not see it. A duplicate type was written and then found by the lib.rs re-export and reverted. A debt that records an absence must record the AXIS of the absence or the round that opens it rebuilds what is there. THE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT THE PROMOTION FIXED: RawGrab kept its OWN copy of the set, seeded EMPTY at the grab's first press, so a raw sink grabbed while another button was already down was told that button was up. One writer, one answer, and the grab's lifetime is now read from the pointer's set rather than from a private mirror. THE RELEASE IS ITSELF AN EVENT REPORTING THE BUTTON UP, which is the round's sharpest finding and it was a real bug for an hour: the coordinator's rule "if the primary button is not held, close the gesture" sat at the top of the handler, so the release tripped it before the sweep could be consumed and EVERY drag collapsed back to one row on mouse-up. The end verdict is now TAKEN and carried down the handler. THE SECOND DEFECT THE DEBT NAMED CLOSED WITHOUT BEING WORKED ON: a release outside the window used to strand a coordinator's re-derived pressed flag forever. There is no flag now -- the state travels with the event, so whatever arrives next closes the gesture. THE WRITER IS IDEMPOTENT ON PURPOSE, so every entry point that represents a button edge notes its own without a census of which of them overlap on a given press; a list would go stale, the property does not. THE 3-TUPLE BECAME A NAMED SendPayload over 79 sites: the wire has grown a segment three times and each growth re-broke every consumer's destructuring, not because the consumer was wrong but because an anonymous tuple has no way to say a fourth fact exists and may be ignored. AN ADJACENT GAP HAD TO CLOSE TOO AND ONLY THE DEMO FOUND IT: R781 put modifiers on the RELEASE only, which held for 838 rounds because every chord-aware widget acted on the activation edge -- and stops holding the moment a gesture BEGINS at a press, because a Ctrl-anchored sweep is a function of the chord held when the finger went down. The unit test passed by feeding the payload directly; the wire could not produce it. The router now caches the shell's absolute modifier state and stamps both axes on every arm. HAND-ROLLED GRAMMAR IS NOT EXEMPT: two split_once(':') decoders broke, a test fixture and hello-scene-scale -- and the latter had ALREADY been silently inert on any Shift-click since R781. 12 counterfactuals, 12 caught, but only after the driver itself was fixed: a killed first run left one file mutated (the R1617 lesson, hit again), the next run started RED, and all eight of its CAUGHT verdicts were void while the summary read 8/12. tools/counterfactual.py now runs the gate once unmutated and refuses a red baseline -- the only failure mode it had that looks like success -- with its own test. Two counterfactuals then PASSED and both were real: nothing in the Rust suite caught the press losing its chord (the demo did, which is the R1618 lesson recurring), and nothing caught the RPC read publishing a constant, because the producer sat between the router suite and the rpc suite and was reached by neither. Both now have tests. A 38-assertion demo drives the whole gesture through the ordinary pointer methods -- no drag-select RPC was invented, because a sweep IS a press and some moves and a special method would let the AI-driven gesture diverge from the physical one. 21 blast-radius demos re-pass. New debt: debt-drag-select-has-no-autoscroll (the reference's abstract item view has an auto-scroll property, an edge-margin property and a start-auto-scroll entry point; the hard part is not the timer but re-resolving hover when content moves under a stationary cursor).

a drag reaches PAST the edge: pinion_core::widgets::scroll::AutoScroll plus InputRouter::tick_auto_scroll plus scene/input_state.auto_scroll close debt-drag-select-has-no-autoscroll, the residue R1619 left one round earlier. Declared `modelview` because the item is the same one R1562 named: a sweep that can only reach what is painted is not the gesture, and every virtualized view in the tree is windowed. THE DEBT NOTE I WROTE ONE ROUND AGO WAS WRONG, AND A TEST SAID SO IN FIVE MINUTES. It claimed the hard part was re-resolving hover when content moves under a stationary cursor, and that the router had no trigger for it. Measured: it does. refresh_hover_for_all_active_pointers runs on every repaint and skips only gesture-PINNED pointers, which a plain drag-select is not -- so scrolling the content mid-sweep already extended the selection ([[0,1]] -> [[0,2]] -> [[0,3]] with the cursor untouched). That is TWO ROUNDS RUNNING where a debt note's diagnosis was false, R1619 on an inherited one and R1620 on its own, one round old. A note written at round-end without a test is a guess, and it costs the next round the time to disprove it. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING was the ramp and the frame tick, and the design parts from the reference on the axis that matters. Read from its source rather than assumed: its counter starts at zero when auto-scroll begins and increments once per timer tick (capped at the page step), and THAT counter is the per-tick distance -- so the speed is a function of elapsed time alone and the pointer's depth into the margin is read as a boolean. A user who wants to go faster cannot; one who overshoots waits for the ramp to restart. Here the band IS a ramp: zero at its inner edge, the declared maximum at the boundary, linear between, saturating outside. Measured over ten identical frames through the wire: 61 px shallow versus 231 px deep. It also deletes a state -- there is no ramp counter to reset, because speed is a pure function of position. And it integrates a velocity against the frame's own dt, where the reference scrolls a fixed step per 50 or 150 ms timer tick (hard-coded, with a source comment wishing it were a style hint). NOTHING IS FABRICATED. The reference makes the selection follow the scroll by SYNTHESISING a mouse-move and posting it to the viewport, an event the application cannot tell from the user's. Here the new hover target is a derivation of the new picture, on a path that already existed -- which is why the probe above mattered: the round leaned on it and proved it first. THE PIN IS THE GESTURE. The region is captured at the press (weakly, with its viewport rect AND its declared policy) because auto-scroll's most useful moment is when the pointer is dragged PAST the edge, and at that moment a hit-test finds nothing. Pinning also makes the gesture belong to ONE region, the way its selection does. The policy is snapshotted too: a default-valued fallback would have switched a region that declared OFF back on at exactly the moment the pin starts being used. A COUNTERFACTUAL MADE THE ROUND DELETE CODE. The tick was gated on both `held_buttons(id).is_empty()` and the pin's presence, and nothing could catch removing the first -- because a pin exists exactly while a button is held, so the two could never disagree. Two readers of one fact, and the fix was to delete a check rather than to test it. Another moved the repeat/auto-scroll composition off the shell and onto the router: `a() || b()` short-circuits and would silently halve a press that is both repeating and scrolling, and the shell had no fixture that could drive both, so the composition went where the R1549 fixtures live and got the test it could not have had. tools/counterfactual.py's own R1619 baseline gate paid for itself immediately. A third found that off() zeroes BOTH the band and the speed, so no test could say which half of is_enabled was load-bearing; a zero-width band with a live speed now has one. 9 counterfactuals, 9 caught, after one was retired as mis-written (its edit was inert because the real gate sits one level down, and the property it named is covered by the pin case). The per-frame shell seam is renamed tick_pointer_hold_for_window: a second continuation arriving under a name that promised only the first is how three backends end up with two seams that drift. A 33-assertion demo drives the whole thing through the ordinary pointer methods and reads the ramp off the wire at four depths on both edges; 12 blast-radius demos re-pass including the auto-repeat one.

a display says how much of it is usable AND how sure it is: pinion_core::display::UsableRegion plus usable_regions plus the pinion-shell _NET_WORKAREA probe plus scene/displays.usable close debt-display-usable-region-unmodelled -- the last BUILDABLE analyzer-tool plane-C gap. Declared `osnative` because it is a window-system integration probe, the same axis R1617 advanced; the gated part of that axis (Mac/Win surfaces) is untouched. THE REFERENCE'S OWN SOURCE IS THE FINDING. Its X11 plugin carries an internal comment saying that deriving a per-monitor work area from the desktop-wide atom is unreliable, that window managers disagree about what the atom means with several monitors attached, and that the WM specification has no atom for the per-monitor answer. Its conclusion is the part that matters: its screen accessor RETURNS THE FULL BOUNDS for every display as soon as more than one is attached, unless an environment variable overrides -- so on any two-monitor desk it answers 'all of it is available' and the caller cannot tell that from a measurement. Two different facts arriving as one value with the difference discarded at the boundary, which is R1617's shape exactly. SO THE ANSWER CARRIES ITS PROVENANCE. Four arms, not Option<Rect>: reported (a measurement), desktop_wide (a work area exists but this desk has several displays and the clip cannot be attributed), unpublished (the platform has none -- Wayland, where the protocol does not tell a client), unprobed (nobody asked). `rect()` answers on every arm so a client placing a window never matches; `is_measured()` is true only for the first. Option<Rect> would have fused 'no panels', 'cannot say' and 'nobody looked' into one absence. AND THE DERIVATION RECOVERS DISPLAYS THE REFERENCE GIVES UP ON. If the desktop work area takes NOTHING from a display, that display's whole bounds are usable and that is a real answer however many displays the desk has -- so a dock down the left monitor leaves the right monitor with a measurement, where the reference loses both. Only the displays the atom actually clips are unattributable. A display the work area misses entirely reports its bounds rather than an empty rect, because 'none of this display can be used' is the one answer certainly wrong. THE PROBE IS REAL AND IT RAN. x11rb was already in the tree transitively via winit, so the dependency is a direct edge rather than a second copy, and it is target-scoped. Measured on this desk through the wire: usable 2494x1568+66+32, reported -- a 66px left dock and a 32px top bar, off the live root window. A Wayland session is refused BEFORE connecting, because under XWayland the atom describes the X root rather than the compositor's panels and answering would be a guess about the wrong desk. Every failure inside the probe collapses to None on purpose: a work area is an optimisation on placement, and a shell that refused to start over a missing property would trade a cosmetic answer for the application. THREE COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED FIRST AND ALL THREE WERE REAL. Nothing caught 'probed-and-empty' collapsing into 'never probed' -- the distinction the type exists for. Nothing caught the wire publishing a constant provenance, and nothing caught the schema's closed value set being hand-written instead of derived from the arms; the demo could catch neither, because a real desk produces one arm out of four. All three now have tests, and the schema test asserts the DECLARED set equals the set the conversion can emit. 10 counterfactuals, 10 caught, from a verified-green baseline. The wire type is declared in pinion-rpc rather than core (the DisplayHomeWire precedent -- the census that keeps rpc/schema honest reads only that crate), and the value set is R1616's `values` slot fed from UsableRegion::WIRE_NAMES, a const derived from the arms. A 20-assertion demo reads the vocabulary off rpc/schema before parsing, checks the region never exceeds its bounds, and asserts the declared set is strictly larger than what this desk produced -- because a single-arm enum would make the provenance decorative. 5 display-family demos re-pass.

the crate stacks: pinion_chart::stack + StackedBand + stacked_value_bounds + draw::area_between + LineChart::stacked pay the chart residue's plainest item -- the crate drew several areas over one another and left the ACCUMULATION to the application. A binding wanting a stacked area chart had to hand in a series whose y was already a running sum, so the chart's tooltips, legend and value axis all reported the TOTAL where the reader sees a band, and the original measurement was gone before anything could ask. That is the shape the standing directive rules out: the deliverable is a crate that composes. THE AUDIT CAME FIRST, BECAUSE THE DEBT FILE DEMANDED IT, AND IT MOVED THE LIST. The file's own How-to-apply says every item is an R1568 judgment to re-check against the code, since its #1-#7 all went stale that way. Measured: the CATEGORY AXIS IS PRESENT (TickFormat::Category(Categories) in ticks.rs) -- that entry was stale. LABEL THINNING exists in some form (a whole-decade stride). LOCAL TIME is absent BY STATED DESIGN, with civil.rs saying it needs a timezone database, which makes it an external dependency rather than a gap. And the per-mark a11y item is MIS-FRAMED: it names box/candle/polar as lacking what others have, but the whole crate has no AccessNode at all, so that is one axis-wide question and not three widget ones. Genuinely absent and correctly framed: OHLC, spline, stacked area, violin, and SVG `d` / Arc-Quad -- and the last of those is a Scene::Path vocabulary axis the file itself says is not really dataviz. STACKING IS TWO CURVES, NOT ONE, which is why area_path could not express it: it closes onto a SCALAR baseline. area_between walks the upper curve forwards and the lower backwards so the ring closes without a bow tie where a negative series crosses. And the band keeps both facts -- Series::points is what was measured, upper/lower is where it is drawn -- so nothing has to reconstruct one from the other. IT REFUSES TO GUESS. Stacking is only defined on a shared x grid: adding a value sampled at 10:00 to one sampled at 10:07 requires deciding what the second was doing at 10:00, and every answer is an interpolation the chart would be inventing. A series whose grid disagrees is drawn UNSTACKED on the baseline rather than resampled, because a picture whose totals are not the data's totals is the one failure a stacked chart must not have. The f64 grid comparison is exact on purpose and says so: these are the same numbers the caller put in, so a tolerance would only admit a genuinely different grid. Negatives stack DOWNWARD from the running total rather than being clamped. A hidden series contributes nothing and draws no band, while the ones above keep their palette index, so a legend toggle re-stacks without re-colouring. THE AXIS DEFECT IS THE ONE A CALLER MEETS FIRST: three series each peaking at 40 reach 120, and a plot scaled to the per-series maximum clips two thirds of the picture. stacked_value_bounds is its own function for that reason, and resolved_y_domain was EXTRACTED from build_body because a counterfactual proved the choice untestable inline -- a test can compare two pictures but cannot say which domain produced either. That extraction is the round's second finding-driven structural change. 8 counterfactuals, 8 caught, from a verified-green baseline; two were rewritten after cargo fmt moved their anchors and one after it did not compile. A 14-assertion demo drives the real binary: hello-chart-fill is now stacked (an area chart of several series is FOR the total), and the demo asserts the bands do not share a baseline -- which overlapping areas necessarily do -- and that they differ in height, so a single merged silhouette would fail. The value axis's extent is checked in Rust rather than in the demo, because reading it back off painted tick text compares an SI-rounded string to a float and would pass for the wrong reason. 3 chart-family demos re-pass.

a path keeps the curve it was authored as: pinion_core::path_data plus PathCommand::QuadTo / ArcTo plus the closed PathSegment form close the analyzer-tool audit's `SVG d parsing / Arc-Quad commands` row -- the last of the chart-residue items that is not a series type, and the one the debt file itself said is really a Scene::Path VOCABULARY axis rather than dataviz. Declared `none` rather than an axis for that reason: no Phase B capability moved, this is the primitive under charting, the catalog and the DCC widgets alike, and crediting one of them would inflate an axis for work it is not named for (R1542's rule, R1606 and R1613's precedent). THE VOCABULARY SURVIVES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. The reference converts on the way IN -- quadTo computes the equivalent cubic and calls cubicTo, arcTo appends Beziers, and the stored element list has four kinds with no arc among them -- so a path there cannot be asked whether it holds a circle, and there is no inverse back to path data. Under 2#7 the scene is what a client READS, so an answer already expanded into a rasterizer's Beziers answers a different question. QuadTo and ArcTo therefore reach the scene, the wire and back out through write(), and the cubic expansion is derived on demand. WHAT IS SHORTHAND IS NOT VOCABULARY, and the line is stated: relative commands, H/V and the smooth S/T are fully determined by what precedes them and are resolved at parse time; a quadratic's DEGREE and an arc's ellipse are not, so those two are kept. THE ENUM COULD NOT GROW SAFELY BEFORE THIS. PathCommand is non_exhaustive and every consumer matched it with a wildcard, so a new arm would have been skipped by the Vello adapter (`_ => {}`) and collapsed to `"Unknown"` on the wire -- painting nothing and introspecting as nothing, with nothing failing. The answer is a second CLOSED type: PathSegment is not non_exhaustive and the only way to obtain one is for_each_segment, whose match is exhaustive inside pinion-core where non_exhaustive does not apply. The wire is closed the same way, by rendering PathCommand::describe's three argument shapes instead of the commands themselves, which is what let the Unknown arm be DELETED rather than extended. The paint hash follows describe too, and that is the arm that mattered most: a hand-written hasher that forgot the sweep flag would give the two halves of a circle ONE hash and the fragment cache would paint one with the other's pixels. THE ERROR CHANNEL IS THE OTHER HALF. The reference's parser answers std::nullopt -- one bit, no position, no cause -- and is unreachable anyway, declared only in private headers, so every application writes its own. Three of its behaviours are silent acceptances rather than errors, each now a named test: data that does not begin with a moveto (it seeds MoveTo(0,0) through ensureData and draws from the origin), a trailing letter with no arguments (the argument array comes back empty, the loop body never runs, and the command vanishes with the path reported valid), and a non-finite number (parsed to infinity, then lineTo/cubicTo bail on !hasValidCoords, warning only in debug builds). Here each is a PathDataError carrying the byte offset, the command letter and the cause. Empty `d` parses to an empty path, which is what SVG says and what the reference calls failure. A COUNTERFACTUAL FOUND A REAL HOLE IN THE ROUND'S OWN TESTS. Replacing F.6.5.2's sign rule `large_arc == sweep` with `large_arc` alone was caught by NOTHING: the arc tests exercised sweep 0/1 at large_arc 0 and large_arc 0/1 at sweep 1, so two of the four flag pairs were never asked, and the sweep test's assertion survived a centre flip. The rule is a statement about all four pairs, so the property is now the pairing itself -- the agreeing pairs share one circle and the differing pairs share the other, with both centres computed in the test from the chord rather than read back out of the code. Cross-checked against the reference's own conversion, which carries the identical rule, so two independent implementations of F.6.5 agree and the defect was the test rather than the code. 12 counterfactuals, 12 caught after that repair, from a verified-green baseline; three were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing. The osnative axis was re-judged 66 -> 69 as the push gate demanded (R1621 moved its evidence past the band): it closes exactly one of the two platform probes R1617 named, and the gate -- Mac/Win native surfaces -- is untouched. 48 path_data tests, a paint-hash test that varies every argument of every command, an RPC census over PathCommandKind::ALL with a fixture per kind, and hello-svg-path importing four real icon `d` strings with a Toggle that swaps in malformed data so the binding REPORTS the byte instead of drawing nothing. A 60-plus-assertion demo drives the real window; r721_path, three chart demos and the donut demo re-pass unchanged.
